item.title: Forges
item.description: Termorq connects to the code forges you already use: GitHub (github.com or GitHub Enterprise Server), GitLab (gitlab.com or self-managed) and Azure DevOps. It shows the work assigned to you, the pull requests waiting for your review and your pipelines, and tells you when one of them needs you. It all runs in the desktop app with your own token. There are no webhooks and no Termorq server.

item.title: Guide map
item.description:
The sidebar is this list. Each group below is a chapter.

Get started link

Install and run, build a local release, the window, and the sample workspace you can run offline.

The terminal link

The prompt and command search including a multiline shell command and coloured shell output with an elapsed time, shells including an exported shell variable in an API credential or an MCP stdio environment row that the prompt does not read as you type, a call that stops before it is sent when that name is missing, and a separate value for each tab and WSL distribution that is dropped from history, exports, recordings, notifications, persisted tabs, trace, and model text, tabs and splits including opening a tab with a chosen shell, a # request that stays on this tab, and disk space from the local folder, the interactive terminal including captured output dropped when you take over a running command and Termorq commands during a program, history, find and export, inline images including a persistent shell command that keeps a TIFF, a clickable path, and one notification for a finished line, and a file dropped on an SSH terminal that is not typed into the session, Markdown runbooks including a block that runs in the file’s directory when the file has one, repo runbooks and Explain a failed command including a task that uses the tab’s host folder, recording and replay including a normal persistent-shell command, with an interactive session left as a gap note, and the drop-down window.
